strengths: The central idea is interesting: directly matching a latent student's KV cache to a compressed teacher cache provides supervision across latent positions and layers, extending CODI's endpoint supervision.

Table 1 reports substantial gains on natural-language traces. On GSM8K, Qwen-0.5B improves from 20.2% with CODI to 44.4%, while Llama-1B achieves 55.7% versus PCCoT's 50.72%. Experiments cover two model families, three model sizes, and two additional arithmetic benchmarks.

The paper includes useful ablations of eviction criteria, loss choices, latent budgets, iterations, and endpoint supervision. Reporting three-seed uncertainty for the smaller models and providing dataset and hyperparameter details are positive.
weaknesses: Baseline tuning is asymmetric, weakening attribution of the improvements to KV supervision. KAVA receives a multidimensional hyperparameter sweep, whereas newly evaluated baselines inherit Llama-1B settings and receive only learning-rate tuning. Several other results are copied from prior work. A controlled, equally tuned PCCoT comparison with only the KV loss toggled is particularly important; Table 3 instead removes CODI supervision, and Table 4 uses the previously reported PCCoT result.

The central cache-alignment operation is underspecified. Independently selecting top-M entries per head and layer does not define their ordering against student latent positions. The paper also does not explain whether keys are matched before or after rotary positional encoding, how differing teacher/student positions are handled, or what happens when a teacher trace contains fewer than M tokens. These choices materially affect the proposed objective.

Efficiency is assessed only through forward-pass counts. A Jacobi pass updating 24 latent positions has a different cost from a single-token decoding pass, so the reported 62–92% reductions do not establish comparable latency or compute savings. There are no measured latency, throughput, peak-memory, or training-cost results. The quadratic key-similarity computation and attention-score extraction also require practical overhead measurements.

The claims of consistent superiority and robustness are overstated. For Llama-3B trained on natural-language traces, SVAMP accuracy falls to 66.1%, below CODI's 70.1%; its equation-to-natural-language drop on GSM8K is 5.7 points versus CODI's 5.1. Llama-1B also trails CODI on equation-trained SVAMP. Evaluation remains confined to closely related arithmetic tasks and models up to 3B, limiting conclusions about complex reasoning and scalability.

The evidence does not sufficiently isolate why compressed KV targets help. There is no random-selection or uniformly spaced-selection control, key-only/value-only comparison, or quantitative demonstration that the selected teacher cache preserves answer performance at the actual latent budget. The qualitative similarity plots concern one example and largely verify the optimized matching objective rather than establish faithful reasoning transfer.

Reproducibility details contain unresolved inconsistencies. Equation 7 specifies L1/MSE while Appendix C frequently uses Smooth L1; loss normalization is not fully defined; Appendix A references pad_tokens before assignment; and the stated universal eviction weight of 0.1 conflicts with the 3B natural-language configuration. The 3B results also lack uncertainty despite the stated three-seed protocol. Together with the evaluation limitations, these issues leave the submission below the acceptance threshold.

strengths: Distilling compressed teacher KV caches into continuous latent states is a plausible, useful extension of endpoint supervision. The paper clearly distinguishes this objective from CODI and integrates it with PCCoT.

Table 1 shows substantial improvements in several settings: Qwen-0.5B GSM8K accuracy with natural-language training rises from 20.2% for CODI to 44.4%, and Llama-1B reaches 55.7% versus 50.72% for PCCoT.

Evaluation covers three backbones, paired equation-only and natural-language training data, and two transfer benchmarks. Ablations investigate supervision components, eviction strategies, loss choices, and latent computation budgets; several results include three-seed uncertainty estimates.
weaknesses: Baseline tuning is asymmetric, weakening attribution of the gains to KV distillation. KAVA receives a broader hyperparameter search, while newly run baselines inherit Llama-1B settings and mainly sweep learning rates. Table 4 provides a useful comparison without KV loss, but its standard-setting PCCoT result comes from prior work. A consistently rerun, equally tuned comparison is especially necessary to explain the very large Qwen gains.

The central alignment procedure is underspecified. Independently selected KV entries must be ordered and assigned to student positions, but the paper does not clearly specify that ordering, positional-encoding treatment, or handling of teacher traces shorter than the latent budget. These choices materially affect the objective. Appendix A also references pad_tokens before defining it, and the layer-wise normalization listed in Appendix C is not sufficiently defined.

Efficiency evidence is inadequate for the deployment claims. Table 2 counts forward passes, although a Jacobi pass processes multiple latent positions and is not equivalent in cost to one cached autoregressive decoding step. There are no measured latency, throughput, peak-memory, or training-cost results. The reduced iteration count is inherited from PCCoT, whose efficiency results are omitted.

Claims of consistent superiority and smaller degradation with natural-language traces overstate Table 1. KAVA trails CODI on Llama-1B equation-trained SVAMP (58.9% versus 61.1%) and Llama-3B natural-language SVAMP (66.1% versus 70.1%). For Llama-3B GSM8K, its equation-to-natural-language drop is also slightly larger than CODI's. These exceptions require explicit discussion.

The evaluation supports a narrower contribution than the claims about complex reasoning and scalability. All tasks are arithmetic word problems, and the largest backbone is 3B. GSM8K-Hard accuracy remains low, while Llama-3B natural-language GSM8K accuracy remains 8.4 points below full CoT. Broader tasks and longer reasoning workloads are needed to substantiate the claimed generality.

Evidence for the proposed mechanism remains limited. The cosine-similarity analysis uses one example and measures alignment explicitly encouraged by the training loss; decoded examples do not establish preservation of reasoning dynamics. Comparisons against simpler pooled or uniformly selected targets and token-aligned intermediate supervision would help establish why independently compressed KV targets matter. Overall, the promising empirical results do not yet overcome the evaluation and reproducibility gaps for a top-tier acceptance.

strengths: Compressed teacher KV caches provide a useful and distinctive supervision target for latent reasoning, extending CODI’s endpoint supervision to intermediate representations.

The strongest empirical gains are substantial: on natural-language GSM8K training, Qwen-0.5B improves from 20.2% with CODI to 44.4%, while Llama-1B improves from 49.7% to 55.7%. Results across two model families support the approach’s promise.
The paired equation-only and natural-language training datasets offer a useful controlled comparison. Evaluation also includes two arithmetic generalization benchmarks.

Ablations examine endpoint supervision, projection, eviction criteria, loss choice, and latent computation budgets. Multiple-seed results for smaller models and detailed hyperparameter tables are helpful.
weaknesses: Baseline comparisons do not fully isolate the contribution. KAVA receives a broader hyperparameter search, whereas reproduced baselines primarily receive learning-rate tuning, and several important comparisons use published results. A controlled PCCoT comparison differing only in the KV loss, with matched tuning and seed budgets across backbones, is needed.

Efficiency is measured only through forward-pass counts. A Jacobi pass updating 24 latent positions costs differently from a single-token decoding pass, so the reported 62–92% reductions do not establish corresponding latency, FLOP, or memory savings. Wall-clock inference and training costs are missing, including the cost of pairwise cache scoring.

Important details of the central matching objective remain unspecified: how independently selected cache entries are ordered for student alignment, whether keys are matched before or after rotary positional encoding, and how traces shorter than the latent budget are handled. Appendix A also references pad_tokens before defining it, while the prose and pseudocode differ on the sign of the redundancy score.

The claims of consistent superiority and reduced natural-language degradation are too broad. On Llama-3B with natural-language training, SVAMP accuracy is 66.1% versus CODI’s 70.1%; its GSM8K decline between training formats is also slightly larger than CODI’s. Llama-1B trails CODI on equation-trained SVAMP, and the 3B results lack reported uncertainty.

The evaluation remains confined to closely related arithmetic tasks and models no larger than 3B. Natural-language traces here are verbalized arithmetic solutions, providing limited evidence for claims about complex, long-horizon reasoning or broad scalability.

The mechanism analysis is suggestive rather than conclusive. Selected decoded examples and cache similarities encouraged directly by the training loss do not establish faithful reasoning transfer. Comparisons with simpler intermediate-state supervision or alternative cache alignment strategies would better substantiate the significance of head-wise compressed KV targets.

strengths: Compressed teacher KV-caches provide a meaningful, technically plausible supervision signal for latent reasoning, extending endpoint distillation to intermediate latent representations.
Table 1 shows substantial improvements in several settings: on natural-language GSM8k, Qwen-0.5B improves from CODI’s 20.2% to 44.4%, and Llama-1B improves from PCCoT’s 51.1% to 55.7%.

Evaluation covers three backbones, multiple mathematical benchmarks, and both equation-only and natural-language traces. Ablations examine eviction criteria, loss functions, latent budgets, iteration counts, training-data quantity, and trace sources.
weaknesses: The efficiency evidence is incomplete. Counting forward passes treats parallel updates of 24 latent tokens as equivalent to single-token decoding. Without latency, throughput, FLOPs, peak memory, or training-cost measurements, the claimed deployment and computational benefits remain insufficiently established.

Central cache-alignment details are unspecified: ordering retained entries across independently pruned heads/layers, handling positional rotations when teacher and student positions differ, and handling traces shorter than the 24-token budget. Appendix A provides scoring pseudocode rather than the full matching procedure and references pad_tokens before defining it.

Baseline comparisons do not consistently control tuning and uncertainty. KAVA receives a broader hyperparameter search, whereas newly evaluated baselines primarily receive learning-rate sweeps. Several results lack repeated-run estimates. MetaMathQA comparisons additionally use different trace preprocessing and report only non-diverged baseline runs without quantifying failure rates.

Evidence for scaling to complex reasoning is limited. Appendix G acknowledges that fully latent MetaMathQA models only slightly outperform answer-only training; stronger results retain substantial explicit reasoning. Experiments stop at 3B parameters and remain confined to mathematics.

Claims of consistent superiority overstate Table 1: for Llama-3B trained on natural-language traces, KAVA achieves 66.1% on SVAMP versus CODI’s 70.1%. The mechanistic interpretation is also weakly supported: qualitative decoding and similarity to directly supervised targets do not establish faithful reasoning or preservation of the teacher’s reasoning dynamics.

strengths: Compressed teacher KV-caches provide a concrete and useful supervision target for latent reasoning. Matching intermediate caches extends the endpoint supervision used by CODI while retaining PCCoT’s inference procedure.

Table 1 provides meaningful evidence of improved accuracy across two model families and three model sizes. On natural-language GSM8K training, KAVA improves GSM8K accuracy from 51.1% to 55.7% over PCCoT for Llama-1B, and from 20.2% to 44.4% over CODI for Qwen-0.5B.

The experimental investigation is substantial: it includes out-of-distribution arithmetic benchmarks, MetaMathQA, eviction and loss ablations, latent-budget experiments, training-data scaling, and alternative trace generators. Several principal results include three-seed uncertainty estimates.
weaknesses: The efficiency evaluation does not establish practical computational savings. Table 2 counts a Jacobi pass updating 24 latent positions as one forward pass, just as it counts a single-token decoding step. Without latency, throughput, FLOPs, peak memory, and hardware measurements, the reported 62–92% reduction in forward passes cannot substantiate the broader efficiency and deployability claims. Training overhead is also unmeasured.

Important details of the central matching operation remain unspecified: how independently selected teacher entries are ordered against student positions, whether keys are matched before or after rotary position encoding, and how traces shorter than the 24-token latent budget are handled. The latter is especially relevant because GSM8K-Aug averages 23.1 reasoning tokens. Appendix A supplies scoring pseudocode rather than a complete alignment algorithm, and references pad_tokens before defining it.

The comparisons do not fully isolate the proposed contribution under equally optimized conditions. KAVA receives a sweep over several loss and normalization choices, whereas newly evaluated baselines primarily receive learning-rate sweeps. MetaMathQA changes both the supervision objective and trace preprocessing between methods, and reports only non-diverged baseline runs without failure rates. Stronger controls would include equally tuned baselines and simple random or uniformly sampled KV targets.

The strongest scalability claims exceed the demonstrated scope. Models stop at 3B parameters, and tasks remain mathematical reasoning. More importantly, Appendix G acknowledges that replacing the entire MetaMathQA trace with latent tokens yields only slight improvements over no-CoT; the stronger results retain substantial explicit reasoning. These hybrid results support a useful accuracy–efficiency trade-off, but do not establish that fully latent inference preserves long-trace reasoning performance.

Claims of consistent superiority need qualification. For Llama-3B trained on natural-language traces, KAVA achieves 66.1% on SVAMP versus CODI’s 70.1%; several Llama-1B equation-only results also fail to improve on the strongest baseline. Uncertainty estimates are missing for the 3B and MetaMathQA comparisons.

The mechanistic interpretation is stronger than its evidence. Cache cosine similarity is expected under the training loss, and selected decoded examples do not demonstrate faithful reasoning or functional equivalence to the compressed teacher cache. Overall, the promising accuracy gains place the paper near the threshold, but unresolved efficiency, reproducibility, and comparison issues leave it marginally below acceptance.

strengths: The paper presents a meaningful extension of latent reasoning: supervising intermediate latent states with a compressed teacher KV-cache. This provides richer guidance than CODI’s endpoint matching and distinguishes the contribution from methods that compress an already-generated cache.

Table 1 provides concrete evidence of effectiveness across two model families and three model sizes. On natural-language GSM8k training, KAVA improves GSM8k accuracy over PCCoT from 51.1% to 55.7% for Llama-1B and from 19.1% to 44.4% for Qwen-0.5B. These gains support the usefulness of the additional supervision.

The evaluation includes equation-only and natural-language traces, transfer benchmarks, and longer MetaMathQA traces. Ablations examine eviction strategies, loss choices, latent budgets, iteration counts, projection, and complementary CODI supervision. Additional experiments investigate training-data quantity and trace generators.

KAVA preserves PCCoT’s inference procedure while improving its accuracy in most reported settings. The main improvements therefore do not require additional inference stages relative to this baseline. Several principal results include three-seed uncertainty estimates.
weaknesses: Practical efficiency remains insufficiently established. Table 2 counts forward passes, although a Jacobi pass updating 24 latent positions has different computational and memory costs from a single-token decoding pass. There are no measured latency, throughput, peak-memory, or training-cost results. The reported 62–92% reduction in forward passes should not be interpreted as an equivalent deployment speedup.

Baseline tuning and uncertainty reporting are uneven. KAVA receives sweeps over several method-specific choices, while newly evaluated baselines largely inherit Llama-1B hyperparameters with learning-rate tuning. Qwen PCCoT performs below No-CoT, making further baseline validation particularly valuable. Llama-3B results and many baseline entries lack uncertainty estimates. For MetaMathQA, reporting only non-diverged baseline runs without failure rates or matched tuning makes the stability advantage difficult to quantify.

Important details of the central KV-matching procedure are underspecified: the ordering of independently selected cache entries, treatment of positional encodings when teacher and student positions differ, and handling of traces shorter than the 24-token latent budget. Appendix A references pad_tokens before defining it and ambiguously applies softmax to an input described as attention scores. Table 6 also contradicts the claim that lambda is always 0.1. These issues weaken reproducibility.

The claims of consistent superiority and broad scalability exceed the evidence. For example, on Llama-3B trained with natural-language traces, KAVA reaches 66.1% on SVAMP versus CODI’s 70.1%. Evaluation remains confined to mathematical reasoning with models no larger than 3B. On MetaMathQA, fully latent reasoning offers only small gains over No-CoT; stronger results retain substantial explicit reasoning.

The mechanism analysis is suggestive rather than conclusive. Selected decoded examples and similarity plots do not establish faithful reasoning or show that independently compressed KV targets are uniquely beneficial. Comparisons against pooled or uniformly sampled cache targets and alternative intermediate-state distillation would better isolate the contribution of the proposed compression and alignment.
